newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to free jail inmates to ease overcrowding.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to free jail inmates to ease overcrowding.

text.p: Colombia plans to release thousands of inmates in the coming weeks in a bid to ease chronic overcrowding in its prisons, authorities said on Wednesday.

Rafael Lamo, director of the National Prisons Institute (INPEC), said about 8,000 convicts would benefit from the early release programme and all would have to have served at least two-thirds of their sentences to qualify.

Anyone convicted of drug trafficking, mass murder or "terrorism" would not be eligible for release, he said. Colombian authorities generally use the term "terrorism" to refer to leftist guerrilla activity.
According to official statistics, Colombia's 168 prisons were built to house a total of 28,332 inmates but currently hold 40,590.
Riots have erupted in several prisons over the past month to press for an end to overcrowding and better living conditions for prisoners.
Lamo, who took over as head of the INPEC this month, has said the government is studying the possibility of building prison ships or leasing them from a foreign supplier.
